hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-01.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-01.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(1,1)$, $D=(0,1)$. Points equidistant from the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ lie on the lines $x=\frac12$ and $y=\frac12$ (the perpendicular bisectors of the sides). By symmetry take $X=\left(\frac12,y\right)$. Then $AX^2=\frac14+y^2=\frac12$, so $y=\pm\frac12$; $y=\frac12$ is the center of the square, so $X=\left(\frac12,-\frac12\right)$ (outside). Then $CX^2=\frac14+\frac94=\frac52$. The case $y=\frac12$ line gives the same by symmetry.

**Answer: $\frac52$**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-02.title: Divisibility
hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-02.body:
$107n$ and $n$ have the same last two digits iff $100\mid106n$, i.e. $50\mid53n$, iff $50\mid n$ (as $\gcd(53,50)=1$). The smallest is $50$.

**Answer: 50**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-03.title: Structure of the pairing
hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-03.body:
There are $9$ animals and $7$ bowls, so exactly $7$ animals get bowls and the remaining $2$ form one dog-cat pair. Choose the dog and the cat: $5\cdot4=20$ ways; the bowls are identical, so the rest is determined.

**Answer: 20**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-07.title: Reciprocal roots
hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-07.body:
The reciprocals $u=\frac1p,\frac1q,\frac1r$ are roots of $2u^3+8u^2-9u+1=0$ (reverse the coefficients). So $e_1=-4$, $e_2=-\frac92$, and $\sum u^2=e_1^2-2e_2=16+9=25$.

**Answer: 25**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-08.title: Base 3
hmmt-feb-2008-gen1-08.body:
In base $3$, the rule appends a digit $0$ or $1$, so $S$ is the set of non-negative integers whose base-$3$ digits are all $0$ or $1$. Those below $2008$ have at most $7$ digits (the largest is $1111111_3=1093$, while any $8$-digit one is at least $3^7=2187$), giving $2^7=128$ numbers including $0$. Excluding $0$: $127$.

**Answer: 127**
